prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer looking downward from an elevated truck or trailer bed (roughly 1 to 1.8 m below head height) containing a pile of mulch, a white tailgate ledge on the left, a grey bucket sitting on the ledge about 1 to 1.3 m away, a resting shovel at the upper right about 1.5 m away, and a second person standing on the lower pavement to the far left about 2.5 to 3.5 m away and roughly 1.5 m from the bucket. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's very bright torso, arms, and legs (0.2 to 0.8 m from the lens) shift as they lift a shovel to dump mulch into the bucket in frame 2, lower the shovel to the right in frames 3 to 5, and reach down with their left hand in frames 4 and 5 to grasp and tilt the bucket within arm's reach (under 0.8 m). During frames 2 and 3, the raised left arm and shovel handle partially occlude the bucket and the tailgate behind them, while the second person on the lower left remains mostly out of the frame with only their legs visible facing toward the trailer. The depth map makes the sharp vertical drop-off from the elevated tailgate edge to the dark background ground far clearer than the cluttered, sun-dappled RGB image alone. However, the map is unreliable inside the concave bucket and across the loose mulch pile on the shovel blade, where depth boundaries flatten out, and the distant person on the dark pavement nearly vanishes into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of the scene across the five frames: a grey bucket mislabelled as a green 'bowl' about 1 to 1.3 m below and to the left of the camera wearer in frames 1 and 5, a small distant container on the upper ground labelled 'bottle' about 3 m away in frame 1, the camera wearer's own torso, legs, and arms as a pink 'person' mask (0.2 to 1.0 m away) in frames 2 through 5, and the second person's lower legs on the far left pavement about 2.5 to 3 m away (1.5 m left of the bucket) in frame 2. As the camera wearer turns slightly rightward and bends forward from frame 2 to frame 5, their pink 'person' mask shifts from a raised left arm holding the shovel (which occludes the bucket in frames 2 and 3) to two downward-extending legs straddling the space beside the green 'bowl' mask as the left hand grasps its rim within arm's reach (0.6 m). Both people have their heads out of view—the camera wearer behind the lens looking down, and the second person cropped at the knees on the left edge facing roughly toward the trailer without a visible head or gaze direction. Compared to the RGB image, the segmentation map isolates the boundary of the camera wearer's torso and limbs from the similarly toned clothing and sunlit mulch in frames 2 to 5. However, it is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the shovels, trailer bed, and mulch in all frames, misses the bucket in frames 2 to 4 and the camera wearer in frame 1, and in frame 2 falsely segments a brown patch of mulch and shadow on the right (1 to 1.5 m away) as an extra 'person'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across the sequence, detecting no yellow body skeletons for either the camera wearer (whose torso and legs occupy the lower foreground 0.2 to 1.0 m below the camera) or the second person standing 2.5 to 3.5 m away on the far-left ground about 1.5 m beyond the bucket. It renders only a single magenta hand skeleton in frame 3—the camera wearer's left hand gripping the wooden shovel handle at roughly 0.4 m in front of and below the chest—and a single magenta hand skeleton in frame 5 gripping the upper rim of the grey bucket about 0.6 m away on the left. Across the five frames, these two detections reflect the camera wearer's left hand moving from lifting and lowering the shovel within arm's reach in frames 1 to 3 to reaching forward and left to grab the bucket in frames 4 and 5, while the right hand holding the shovel lower down on the right (0.7 to 1.0 m away) goes undetected. Because both people's heads and upper torsos are out of the field of view or self-occluded by the steep downward egocentric angle, the map provides no head or torso keypoints to indicate facing or gaze direction. While the pose map precisely localizes the articulated finger joints of the left hand gripping the shovel shaft in frame 3 and the bucket rim in frame 5 despite harsh sunlight in the RGB, it is severely unreliable everywhere else, failing to detect all body limbs and missing both hands entirely in frames 1, 2, and 4.
